question: why do lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated charging cycles
note: Held-out set, never tuned on. Three web-search agents: home field (battery), same-shape distant fields, lexical traps. Labels by title from a blind annotator: on / near (same shape, other field) / off.

papers.title: Review of State-of-the-Art Degradation Models for Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Reviews degradation models for lithium-ion batteries. Major degradation mechanisms include formation and growth of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), lithium plating, and loss of active electrode material. These map onto degradation modes: loss of cyclable lithium, loss of active materials, and loss of electrolyte.

papers.title: Degradation in Li-ion batteries and capacity decline under different cycling conditions: A comprehensive review
papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of Li-ion degradation and capacity decline under different cycling conditions. Loss of cyclable lithium often dominates total capacity loss and is typically linked to SEI surface film formation on graphite anodes. Lithium plating occurs with fast charging or low temperature and reacts with electrolyte to form additional SEI.

papers.title: State-of-the-art review of degradation mechanisms of commercial lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Review of degradation mechanisms in commercial lithium-ion cells. Mechanical loss of active material reduces active surface area, so remaining material carries higher interfacial current density, accelerating SEI growth and particle cracking.

papers.title: A Single Particle Model with Electrolyte and Side Reactions for degradation of lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Physics-based single particle model extended with electrolyte dynamics and side reactions to simulate degradation of lithium-ion batteries such as SEI growth and lithium plating.

papers.title: The importance of degradation mode analysis in parameterising lifetime prediction models of lithium-ion battery degradation
papers.abstract: Many combinations of degradation mechanisms can produce the same patterns of capacity and power fade, making it impossible to find a unique validated solution from capacity data alone. Three models of differing complexity all fit capacity and resistance well, but only the model with five coupled mechanisms also fit degradation modes at all temperatures. Validating only against capacity and power fade is stated to be no longer sufficient.

papers.title: Lithium-ion battery degradation: using degradation mode analysis to validate lifetime prediction modelling
papers.abstract: Predicting lithium-ion battery lifetime is described as one of the greatest unsolved problems in battery research. Most prediction papers validate against remaining capacity, but different mechanism combinations give the same fade, so no unique solution exists. Degradation mode analysis (LLI, LAM at both electrodes, electrode slippage) is proposed as validation.

papers.title: Peak-tracking method to quantify degradation modes in lithium-ion batteries via differential voltage and incremental capacity
papers.abstract: Uses peak signatures in voltage and capacity differentials with an open-circuit voltage model and optimization routines to quantify degradation modes. IC and DV analyses are effective for monitoring battery health, though diagnosis often requires considerable parameterization effort and low scan rates.

papers.title: Degradation mechanisms and differential curve modeling for non-invasive diagnostics of lithium cells: An overview
papers.abstract: Overview of degradation mechanisms and their cell-level consequences (degradation modes: conductivity loss, loss of active material, loss of lithium inventory). Presents differential curves as non-invasive, straightforward diagnostic and prognostic tools, alongside pOCV, IC-DV, EIS and differential thermal voltammetry.

papers.title: Rate dependency of incremental capacity analysis (dQ/dV) as a diagnostic tool for lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Quantifies via peak detection how charge/discharge rate affects ICA on two cells. ICA normally needs low constant currents to limit resistance and diffusion effects, which is unfeasible for EV charging. Introduces a faster ICA that corrects peak shift using SOC-dependent resistance from current interrupt. Accuracy of ICA reduces at higher C-rates; C/6 is reported as optimum.

papers.title: Degradation mode estimation using reconstructed open circuit voltage curves from multi-year home storage field data
papers.abstract: Reconstructs the OCV curve continuously over battery lifetime from eight years of operational data of 21 home storage systems (LMO/NMC blend, NMC, LFP). ICA and DVA are applied for degradation mode estimation. Loss of lithium inventory is dominant, while LAM at negative and positive electrodes may be present in some cases.

papers.title: Identifiability Study of Lithium-Ion Battery Capacity Fade Using Degradation Mode Sensitivity for a Minimally and Intuitively Parametrized Electrode-Specific Cell Open-Circuit Voltage Model
papers.abstract: Re-parametrizes a full-cell OCV model by N/P and Li/P ratios and derives gradients of electrode slippage and OCV with respect to LLI and LAM parameters. Characterizes four regimes of degradation identifiability and uses Fisher information to identify informative SOC windows for degradation mode estimation.

papers.title: Phantom LAM and LLI: Resistance and Hysteresis Bias in Voltage-Curve Degradation Mode Analysis
papers.abstract: Degradation mode analysis decomposes capacity fade into LLI and LAM from low-rate voltage-capacity data, but the measured trace includes ohmic drop and charge-discharge hysteresis (notably in graphite-silicon oxide). These can create 'Phantom LAM/LLI', apparent material loss produced by curve registration, branch choice and voltage-windowing rather than true degradation. Tested on LG M50T and Molicel P45B cells with an IR correction.

papers.title: Critical review of non-invasive diagnosis techniques for quantification of degradation modes in lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Critical review of pOCV, IC-DV, EIS and differential thermal voltammetry for quantifying conductivity loss, LAM and LLI, focused on strengths and weaknesses for automotive use. BMSs currently do not indicate the underlying degradation modes. Pseudo-OCV and IC-DV are found more advantageous than EIS and DTV.

papers.title: Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation
papers.abstract: Generates a dataset of 124 commercial LFP/graphite cells under fast charging with cycle lives from 150 to 2,300. Uses discharge voltage curves from early cycles with machine learning; best models reach 9.1% test error predicting cycle life from the first 100 cycles and 4.9% error classifying from the first 5 cycles. Capacity fade is negligible in the first 100 cycles and alone is not a good predictor.

papers.title: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning
papers.abstract: Optimizes six-step ten-minute fast-charging protocols for maximum cycle life using an early-outcome predictor and Bayesian optimization. Needed because testing a single cell to failure under fast charging takes about 40 days and many parameters must be optimized.

papers.title: "Knees" in lithium-ion battery aging trajectories
papers.abstract: Reviews rapid nonlinear degradation ('knees') that severely limits lifetime. Discusses six knee pathways: lithium plating, electrode saturation, resistance growth, electrolyte and additive depletion, percolation-limited connectivity, and mechanical deformation, some with internal state trajectories that are electrochemically undetectable. Notes challenges for knee modeling and prediction.

papers.title: State-of-Health Estimation for Li-Ion Batteries of Real-World Electric Vehicles: Progress, Challenges, and Prospects
papers.abstract: Reviews SoH estimation for real-world EVs. Most work is laboratory-based, leaving a gap to deployment; real batteries face dynamic loads, irregular charging and varied environments. SoH estimation is affected by data heterogeneity, environmental variability and label uncertainty.

papers.title: Reviewing Practical Challenges in Estimating the State-of-Health of Lithium-Ion Batteries from Field Battery Data
papers.abstract: Highlights limitations of laboratory data and reviews practical challenges of field battery data for SoH estimation. Field data quality is far from ideal and incompatible with most state-of-the-art data-driven techniques. Challenges: bridging lab to real conditions, more reliable SoH labeling, less dependence on large training data.

papers.title: State of Health Estimation and Battery Management: A Review of Health Indicators, Models and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Review of health indicators, models and machine learning for SOH estimation. Existing methods are highly data dependent with insufficient physical interpretability and limited cross-scenario generalization; the relation between degradation mechanisms and health indicators is not fully explored.

papers.title: An accelerated aging test procedure for lithium-ion battery based on a dual-temperature approach
papers.abstract: Charging at 20 C and discharging at 40 C replicates normal aging at 25 C with acceleration factor above 5 or even 8. Aims to preserve the aging mechanisms of normal conditions; mechanistic consistency is confirmed with incremental capacity analysis.

papers.title: Accelerated aging protocols design for Li-ion batteries based on equivalence of the degradation mechanisms
papers.abstract: Decouples LLI and positive-electrode active material loss in normal aging, then combines single accelerated protocols by their mechanism proportions. Notes that simply raising stress ignores mechanisms, and the same capacity attenuation does not mean the same state of health when mechanisms differ. Reports acceleration of 62x and 39x under extreme and gentle conditions.

papers.title: Chemistry-aware battery degradation prediction under simulated real-world cyclic protocols
papers.abstract: Notes that existing prediction frameworks rely on rigid unchanging protocols that fail to capture real-world dynamics. Combines hidden Markov processes for realistic power simulation, automated batch testing, an XPS-derived interfacial chemistry database and machine learning to predict degradation under randomized conditions.

papers.title: Lithium-ion battery degradation: Introducing the concept of reservoirs to design for lifetime
papers.abstract: Frames degradation as depletion of finite interacting reservoirs (lithium, porosity, electrolyte) using a DFN model with SEI growth, lithium plating, cracking and solvent dry-out. Over 1,000 cycles, 1% more electrolyte or 5% more porosity extends life by over 30%; excess lithium can accelerate failure without structural or ionic buffers.

papers.title: A generalized Paris' law for fatigue crack growth
papers.abstract: Proposes a generalized form of Paris' law for fatigue crack growth. Paris' law is a log-linear relation between the stress intensity factor range and crack growth rate per cycle, valid in the middle (Region II) regime. Search summary notes the law can significantly underestimate the growth rate of short cracks.
papers.venue: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids

papers.title: Unusual Fatigue Crack Growth Behavior of Long Cracks at Low Stress Intensity Factor Ranges
papers.abstract: Examines fatigue crack growth of long cracks at low stress intensity factor ranges, where behavior departs from the standard Paris regime (Region I). Relevant because the Paris law is often not properly used for life prediction when most fatigue life is spent in Region I.

papers.title: Corrosion-Fatigue Crack Growth in Plates: A Model Based on the Paris Law
papers.abstract: Presents a model of corrosion-fatigue crack growth in plates built on the Paris law, coupling an environmental (corrosion) contribution with cyclic loading crack growth.

papers.title: Bayesian Updating of Fatigue Crack Growth Parameters for Failure Prognosis of Miter Gates
papers.abstract: Updates fatigue crack growth parameters with Bayesian inference to support failure prognosis of miter gates. Illustrates fitting a physics-based crack growth law with observed data to predict failure.

papers.title: Bayesian model updating and prognosis of fatigue crack growth
papers.abstract: Bayesian model updating and prognosis framework for fatigue crack growth, combining a physical crack growth model with monitoring data to predict remaining life.

papers.title: Dual crack growth prognosis by using a mixture proposal particle filter and on-line crack monitoring
papers.abstract: Uses a mixture proposal particle filter with on-line crack monitoring to prognose the growth of two cracks. Particle filters track crack evolution and predict remaining useful life. A noted challenge is that priors far from true values can give correct RUL prognosis but incorrect parameter estimation ('Coordinated Change').

papers.title: Non-Linear Probabilistic Modification of Miner's Rule for Damage Accumulation
papers.abstract: Modifies Miner's linear damage accumulation rule with a nonlinear, probabilistic formulation. Miner's rule assumes damage is linear in cycle ratio and independent of load history; search summaries note it ignores load sequence and load interaction effects, lowering accuracy under variable amplitude loading.

papers.title: Fatigue damage assessment of bogie frame based on an improved nonlinear cumulative damage model
papers.abstract: Proposes an improved nonlinear cumulative damage model for fatigue assessment of a railway bogie frame, addressing the limits of the linear Miner rule, which ignores loading sequence and load interactions.

papers.title: Bayesian and likelihood inferences on remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under gamma process
papers.abstract: Develops likelihood and Bayesian inference for remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under a gamma process, with a random rate change time. Gamma processes model monotone degradation data.

papers.title: Remaining useful lifetime estimation and noisy gamma deterioration process
papers.abstract: Estimates remaining useful lifetime when the gamma deterioration process is observed with noise (measurement error).

papers.title: A common random effect induced bivariate gamma degradation process with application to remaining useful life prediction
papers.abstract: Develops a gamma-process model for bivariate dependent degradation data, where dependency between the two degradation processes is captured by a common random effect, and applies it to remaining useful life prediction.

papers.title: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for gamma degradation process
papers.abstract: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for a gamma degradation process, updating the posterior as new degradation data arrive.

papers.title: Degradation data analysis and remaining useful life estimation: A review on Wiener-process-based methods
papers.abstract: Reviews Wiener-process-based methods for degradation data analysis and RUL estimation. Advantages: degradation paths need not be strictly monotonic under noise, and first-hitting-time gives closed-form failure time expressions.

papers.title: A Wiener-process-based degradation model with a recursive filter algorithm for remaining useful life estimation
papers.abstract: Uses a recursive filter to update the drift coefficient of a Wiener process and the EM algorithm to update all other parameters whenever new degradation data become available, to estimate remaining useful life.

papers.title: Three-Stage Wiener-Process-Based Model for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of a Cutting Tool in High-Speed Milling
papers.abstract: Three-stage Wiener-process model for RUL prediction of a cutting tool in high-speed milling, reflecting distinct wear phases.

papers.title: Photovoltaic Degradation Rates - an Analytical Review
papers.abstract: Reviews degradation rates of flat-plate terrestrial modules and systems from 40 years of field testing; compiles nearly 2000 rates with a median of 0.5%/year, with a historical outline, analytical summary and bibliography by technology.

papers.title: Determinants of the long-term degradation rate of photovoltaic modules: A meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Meta-analysis of PV module degradation rates finding mean and median of 1.1%/year and 0.94%/year, higher than earlier reviews. Meta-regression suggests cell technology, climate, mounting location and measurement method drive differences in reported rates, i.e. reported rates are not comparable across methods.

papers.title: A Deep Learning Model for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aircraft Turbofan Engine on C-MAPSS Dataset
papers.abstract: Deep learning model predicting remaining useful life of aircraft turbofan engines on NASA's C-MAPSS run-to-failure simulation dataset. Related work uses a piecewise linear RUL target.

papers.title: Advancements in bearing remaining useful life prediction methods: a comprehensive review
papers.abstract: Reviews bearing RUL prediction across four aspects: data acquisition, health indicator construction, RUL algorithm development and evaluation. Categorizes algorithms as physical-based, statistical-based and data-driven.

papers.title: Lifetime Prediction Methods for Degradable Polymeric Materials - A Short Review
papers.abstract: Reviews lifetime prediction for degradable polymers: Arrhenius, time-temperature superposition, WLF and isoconversional methods. Limitation: TTSP assumes thermorheological simplicity, which fails near phase transitions such as Tg.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Paradigm for Polymer Aging Lifetime Prediction: Integrating Multi-Mechanism Coupling and Cross-Scale Modeling
papers.abstract: Argues the core limitation of the Arrhenius approach is that it isolates temperature as the dominant variable, whereas real polymers degrade under coupled heat, oxygen, moisture, light and stress, with activation energy modulated nonlinearly by multi-mechanism coupling; proposes machine-learning-based lifetime prediction.

papers.title: Atmospheric corrosion prediction: a review
papers.abstract: Reviews models for predicting atmospheric corrosion. Search summary: the basic power-function kinetic model is accurate for short-term corrosion, but long-term corrosion is better described by linear models accounting for protective corrosion product layers.

papers.title: Long-term prediction of metal corrosion losses in atmosphere using a power-linear function
papers.abstract: Proposes a power-linear function to predict long-term metal corrosion loss in the atmosphere, combining a power-law early stage with a linear later stage.

papers.title: Service life prediction models for chloride-laden concrete
papers.abstract: Compares service life prediction models for chloride-induced corrosion of reinforced concrete (Life-365, CHLODIF, ClinConc, DuraCrete); search summary notes not all models suit all cases, especially advanced concrete under complex environments. Initiation time uses Fick's second law.

papers.title: Essential structure of S-N curve: Prediction of fatigue life and fatigue limit of defective materials and nature of scatter
papers.abstract: Analyzes the structure of the S-N curve for defective materials, predicting fatigue life and fatigue limit and explaining the nature of scatter by combining crack growth with statistics of extremes of defects.

papers.title: Working memory assessment using cambridge neuropsychological test automated battery can help in the diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of CANTAB working memory tests in mild cognitive impairment. Significant differences between MCI patients and healthy controls were found in spatial working memory, spatial span, and rapid visual information processing.
topic_path: neuropsychological test battery for MCI diagnosis

papers.title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Neuropsychological Test Battery in Individuals with Normal Cognition, Mild Cognitive Impairment, or Mild to Moderate Alzheimer's Disease: Results from a Longitudinal Study
papers.abstract: The Neuropsychological Test Battery (NTB) combines widely used clinical tests of memory and executive function, designed to overcome limitations of the ADAS-Cog. It showed high reliability in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and MCI, with decline in mean subtest scores observed at weeks 13, 26, 52 and 78.
topic_path: psychometric validation of a cognitive test battery

papers.title: Examining the Consequences of Neuropsychological Test Battery Changes on Measuring Cognitive Decline
papers.abstract: Examines how changes to neuropsychological test batteries in long-running aging studies affect estimates of cognitive decline. When item response theory scoring is used, changes in test batteries over time may not meaningfully affect estimates of cognitive decline.
topic_path: measurement harmonization in cognitive aging studies

papers.title: Working memory test battery for young adults: Computerized working memory assessment
papers.abstract: Presents a computerized working memory test battery for young adults. Paper describes assessment of working memory capacity components.

papers.title: Long-term lithium therapy and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia: a cohort study
papers.abstract: Cohort study of long-term lithium therapy (a psychiatric mood stabilizer) and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia. Large-scale epidemiological studies have shown that lithium treatment elevates the risk of chronic kidney disease.

papers.title: Lithium nephrotoxicity
papers.abstract: Review of kidney toxicity of lithium in patients treated for bipolar disorder. Lithium enters collecting duct principal cells via the epithelial sodium channel and disrupts vasopressin-regulated water handling by downregulating aquaporin-2.

papers.title: Lithium in Bipolar Disorder: Renal Mechanisms, Nephrotoxicity Phenotypes, and a Shared-Care Pathway for Clinical Practice
papers.abstract: Reviews renal mechanisms and nephrotoxicity phenotypes of lithium in bipolar disorder. Risk is amplified by episodes of lithium intoxication, dehydration, interacting medications, longer treatment duration and comorbid kidney disease.

papers.title: Impact of Long-Term Lithium Treatment on Renal Function in Patients With Bipolar Disorder Based on Novel Biomarkers
papers.abstract: Studies renal function in patients on long-term lithium treatment for bipolar disorder using novel biomarkers.

papers.title: Optimal siting and sizing of electric vehicle charging stations
papers.abstract: Introduces an optimization process for sizing and siting of EV charging stations using graph theory, with the objective of minimizing the integrated cost of charging stations and consumers.

papers.title: Economic planning of electric vehicle charging stations considering traffic constraints and load profile templates
papers.abstract: Determines siting and sizing of charging stations using origin-destination traffic flow data to determine capacity, then integrates charging demand into a cost-based model to evaluate economics of candidate plans.

papers.title: Robust Optimisation for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Siting Under Demand Uncertainty: A Multi-Station Network Planning Model
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer linear programming model that handles demand uncertainty and jointly optimizes selection of candidate sites, fractional demand allocation across stations, and reserve capacity for worst-case demand deviations.
papers.venue: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability

papers.title: Charging Station Siting and Capacity Determination Based on a Generalized Least-Cost Model of Traffic Distribution
papers.abstract: Charging station siting and capacity determination based on a generalized least-cost model of traffic distribution.

papers.title: Carrying capacity reconsidered
papers.abstract: Assesses the utility of the carrying capacity concept and develops an alternative understanding of population growth. Criticizes evidence supposed to support carrying capacity; suggests it may be a self-validating belief with limited relevance to human population growth. Critics note that if conceived as static it is empirically vacuous, and if variable, theoretically incoherent.

papers.title: Carrying capacity reconsidered: from Malthus' population theory to cultural carrying capacity
papers.abstract: Reconsiders carrying capacity from Malthus' population theory to cultural carrying capacity in ecological economics.

papers.title: Formulating variable carrying capacity by exploring a resource dynamics-based feedback mechanism underlying the population growth models
papers.abstract: Formulates a variable carrying capacity through a resource dynamics-based feedback mechanism underlying population growth models.

papers.title: Excess Capacity and Demand-Driven Business Cycles
papers.abstract: Builds a macroeconomic model showing that in an economy where capacity is generally in excess, demand shocks can be the main driving forces of business cycles. Capacity is never fully utilized at the aggregate level.

papers.title: Capacity utilization, superior information, and the business cycle
papers.abstract: Studies business cycle fluctuations of capacity utilization in a factor-hoarding environment with superior information and shows this environment offers a good explanation of the fluctuations of utilization.

papers.title: Investment, Capacity Utilization, and the Real Business Cycle
papers.abstract: Adopts the view that shocks to the marginal efficiency of investment are important for business fluctuations in a neoclassical framework with endogenous capacity utilization.

papers.title: The cell cycle: a review of regulation, deregulation and therapeutic targets in cancer
papers.abstract: Review of cell cycle regulation by cyclins, cyclin-dependent kinases and checkpoints, its deregulation and therapeutic targets in cancer.

papers.title: CDK4: a master regulator of the cell cycle and its role in cancer
papers.abstract: Reviews CDK4 as a regulator of the cell cycle. CDKs are holoenzymes of a cyclin regulatory subunit and a kinase catalytic subunit, activated by cyclin binding and T-loop phosphorylation.

papers.title: Overcharging
papers.abstract: Legal scholarship on prosecutorial overcharging, which is most often practiced to coerce a guilty plea. Horizontal overcharging involves multiple charges from a single incident; vertical overcharging applies more than one similar statute with disparate sentences. Strategic overcharging undermines the Sixth Amendment right to trial.

papers.title: Inside the Black Box of Prosecutor Discretion
papers.abstract: Empirical law review study of prosecutor discretion in charging decisions.

papers.title: Lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia: Epidemiological Findings from National Data Base of Japan
papers.abstract: Epidemiological study of lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia in Japan. Reviews describe such epidemiological studies as inconclusive because of indirect evidence.

papers.title: Effects of mental fatigue on the capacity limits of visual attention
papers.abstract: Examines how mental fatigue from time-on-task affects capacity limits of visual attention. Prolonged task performance typically produces mental fatigue and performance decrements, attributed to depletion of attentional resources, though reductions in motivation likely also play a role.
